_what: Every shape one half of a check's Pass / Fail line can take, as the fixture that produces it and the line it must draw. THE DEFINITION, not a description of one: tools/GameHarness turns each row into an in-game suite, and tests/branch_shapes.rs runs the same row through the engine over the shipped index. Adding a row adds a test to both; neither side declares anything of its own.
_colours: orange = unseen in any game, red = unseen this game, darkRed = already read in this save. A marker is one of those three, or gaveUp for a search that did not finish, or absent where nothing beyond the destination outranks it.
_extra: A row is the whole scenario, and both executors read all of it. If one ever needs something the other cannot use - an in-game screenshot reference, say - it goes under a key naming the executor, 'offline' or 'inGame', so a reader can see at a glance which half of the world it belongs to. NOTHING NEEDS THAT YET and no support for it is built; what the offline executor needs beyond these fields, it reads from the same save the in-game one loads.
_eight: orange alone (nothing outranks the top rung, so it never carries a marker); red alone, red+orange, red+gaveUp; darkRed alone, darkRed+red, darkRed+orange, darkRed+gaveUp. Rows both differ across the two halves and match, which is what says the halves are read separately.
_checks: GROUPED BY THE CHECK THE LINE IS DRAWN ON rather than listed flat. A shape is a property of the line the mod draws, and a line drawn on a WHITE check and one drawn on a RED check are drawn by the same code onto different bands - so a shape that only ever appeared on one of them was a shape nobody had seen the mod put on the other.
_halves: AND PER HALF, NOT PER CHECK, which is the stronger claim and the one the coverage test makes. A check's rows used to be counted with Pass and Fail thrown into one set, so all eight could be present while the FAIL half only ever took the three bare colours - which is exactly what had happened: every markered shape in the table was on a Pass half, and the mod's Fail half had never been seen drawing an asterisk of any kind. Each check now says what each of its halves can take, and the test holds it to that in both directions: a half that claims 'eight' and produces seven fails, and a half that claims 'colours' and produces a marker fails too, since that would mean the graph changed underneath the claim.
_coverage: 'eight' means every shape in _eight. 'colours' means orange, red and darkRed and NEVER a marker - which is not a gap in the fixtures but a fact about the check: a marker reports something beyond where the half lands that outranks it, so a half landing somewhere with nothing beyond it can never carry one.

checks._fail: FAILING LANDS ON TWO ENTRIES, 9:42 and 9:19, with a subtree past them - so this check is the one that can put every shape on a Fail half, and the five rows named fan-fail-* are what do it. Read off the engine: `--branches-of 50` reports 'Fail leads to 9:42, 9:19'.
checks._gaveUp: A ROW THAT WANTS A GIVE-UP MUST RECORD THE CHECK ITSELF, which is why the two fan-fail-*-gives-up rows record 9:50 where their budget-0 twins do not. The bridge answers a start that already carries the class being hunted WITHOUT SEARCHING - 'the start is a result like any other', and a check no save has displayed outranks its own outcome - so with 9:50 left unseen the answer comes back complete and orange having asked nothing, and no state budget can starve a search that never runs. Both rows were written without it first and both drew a found marker instead of a grey one.
